Wikidata has entry Hypholoma fasciculare (Q752507) with data related to this item.

Sulphur Tuft (Hypholoma fasciculare) in the northern Bienwald forest near Jockgrim. The mushroom was growing in clusters on a heavily decayed tree stump in a corner populated exclusively by conifers, mostly pines. The gills have the olive-green tint typical of this species; cap diameter approx. 2 cm, height approx. 6 cm.

 This image was created with Helicon Focus.

ImageDescription.value: Hypholoma fasciculare, commonly known as the sulphur tuft or clustered woodlover, is a common woodland mushroom, often in evidence when hardly any other mushrooms are to be found. This saprotrophic small gill fungus grows prolifically in large clumps on stumps, dead roots or rotting trunks of broadleaved trees.
